title: Present Perfect Continuous
ringkas: have/has been + V-ing, lama kegiatan, dan beda dengan present perfect
goals: membentuk **present perfect continuous** dengan have/has been + V-ing
menjelaskan **lama kegiatan** yang masih berlangsung atau baru selesai
memakai **for, since, all day, lately** dengan tepat

lesson.text: **Present perfect continuous** menekankan **kegiatan** dan **berapa lama** kegiatan itu berlangsung. Cocok untuk menjelaskan sesuatu yang masih berlangsung, atau yang baru saja berhenti dan hasilnya terlihat.

lesson.title: 1. Rumus
table: [[I have been waiting.]] / [[She has been waiting.]]

lesson.title: 2. Dua pemakaian
table: [[I have been studying for two hours.]]
Aku sudah belajar dua jam (dan masih).
[[I am tired. I have been running.]]
Aku lelah karena baru saja berlari.

lesson.title: 3. Bedanya dengan present perfect
table: [[I have been reading this book.]] (kegiatan, mungkin belum selesai)
[[She has been painting the room.]] (kegiatan, ada cat di bajunya)
durasi: [[I have been writing for an hour.]]

lesson.title: Kata kerja keadaan tidak dipakai
lesson.text: Seperti continuous lainnya, kata kerja keadaan tidak dipakai: katakan [[I have known her for ten years.]], bukan ~~I have been knowing her~~. Dan untuk jumlah, pakai present perfect: [[I have written three emails.]]

Budi: Maaf aku terlambat. Apakah kamu sudah menunggu lama?
Anna: Ya, aku sudah menunggu selama empat puluh menit!
Budi: Empat puluh menit? Hujan turun sejak pagi, jadi lalu lintasnya buruk.
Anna: Aku sedang membaca buku, jadi tidak terlalu buruk.
Budi: Kamu membaca apa?
Anna: Aku sedang membaca novel misteri. Aku sudah membaca dua ratus halaman.

read.text:
Budi: Sorry I'm late. Have you been waiting long?
Anna: Yes, I have been waiting for forty minutes!
Budi: Forty minutes? It has been raining since morning, so the traffic is terrible.
Anna: I have been reading a book, so it wasn't too bad.
Budi: What have you been reading?
Anna: I have been reading a mystery novel. I have read two hundred pages already.
read.title: Waiting for the Bus

read.text: Rina has been training for a marathon since January. She has been running five kilometers every morning, and she has been eating healthy food. Her coach says she has improved a lot. She has run two hundred kilometers so far. She is tired today because she has been training for three hours. She hopes the race will go well.

read.text:
Rani: You look tired. What have you been doing?
Tom: I've been studying for the exam since six this morning.
Rani: Have you been eating properly?
Tom: Not really. I've been drinking too much coffee.
Rani: How long have you been sleeping so little?
Tom: For about a week. I've been staying up late every night.
